source_refs.note: Exercise 14.1, Question 12: book page 267 (PDF 272); answer key PDF 311 (book page 306).

blocks.prompt: 12 (i) Which of the following triple can be the direction angles of a single vector: \(45^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\)?
blocks.explanation:
Direction angles koi bhi teen angles nahi ho sakte. Un ke cosines unit vector ke components hain, aur unit vector ki lambai 1 hoti hai, is liye \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\) hona zaroori hai.
Diya kya hai? Teen angles.
Plan: teeno ke cosines ka square, phir jama. Jama bilkul 1 ho to "haan", warna "nahi".
Dhyan dein: angles ko khud jama karna (jaise \(45 + 45 + 60\)) ka is test se koi taluq nahi; hamesha cosines ke squares jama kijiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: angles \(45^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\).
Humein find karna hai: kya yeh ek vector ke direction angles ho sakte hain.
Tareeqa: \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\) wala test (14.1.8 ka Important Result).

Cosines ke squares
\[\cos^2 45^{\circ} = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\cos^2 60^{\circ} = \tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{4} = \tfrac{5}{4}\]
Kyun: Yaad rakhiye: \(\cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\cos 45^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\). Square karne par \(\frac{3}{4}\), \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(\frac{1}{4}\) bante hain.

Jama kar ke faisla
\[\text{Sum} = \tfrac{5}{4} \neq 1\]
Kyun: Jama 1 nahi, is liye koi bhi vector yeh teeno angles ek saath nahi bana sakta. Teen angles apni marzi se nahi chune ja sakte; un mein yeh rishta hona zaroori hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(45^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) kisi ek vector ke direction angles nahi ban sakte (cosines ke squares ka jama \(= \tfrac{5}{4}\)).

blocks.prompt: 12 (iii) Which of the following triple can be the direction angles of a single vector: \(45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\)?
blocks.explanation:
Direction angles koi bhi teen angles nahi ho sakte. Un ke cosines unit vector ke components hain, aur unit vector ki lambai 1 hoti hai, is liye \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\) hona zaroori hai.
Diya kya hai? Teen angles.
Plan: teeno ke cosines ka square, phir jama. Jama bilkul 1 ho to "haan", warna "nahi".
Dhyan dein: angles ko khud jama karna (jaise \(45 + 45 + 60\)) ka is test se koi taluq nahi; hamesha cosines ke squares jama kijiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: angles \(45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\).
Humein find karna hai: kya yeh ek vector ke direction angles ho sakte hain.
Tareeqa: \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\) wala test (14.1.8 ka Important Result).

Cosines ke squares
\[\cos^2 45^{\circ} = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\cos^2 60^{\circ} = \tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{4} + \tfrac{1}{4} = 1\]
Kyun: Yaad rakhiye: \(\cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\cos 45^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\). Square karne par \(\frac{3}{4}\), \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(\frac{1}{4}\) bante hain.

Jama kar ke faisla
\[\text{Sum} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Jama bilkul 1 hai, is liye yeh teen angles kisi ek vector ke direction angles ho sakte hain.

Tasdeeq: ek asal vector
\[\underline{r} = \sqrt{2}\,\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\]
\[|\underline{r}| = \sqrt{2 + 1 + 1} = 2\]
\[\cos\alpha = \tfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\ \cos\beta = \cos\gamma = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \cos 45^{\circ}\) aur \(\frac{1}{2} = \cos 60^{\circ}\). Yani yeh vector sach mein \(45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) ke direction angles rakhta hai, to jawab pakka hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) kisi ek vector ke direction angles ban sakte hain (cosines ke squares ka jama \(= 1\)).
Isi liye sirf (iii) sahi triple hai.
